one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05. No Broadcom print: Q4 FY26 is reported after the close on Wed 2026-12-09 [2], outside the window. In-window events are sector-level: Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 results in late October with the first numeric 2027 capex guides (every clean 2026 guide went up per the house capex file [12], so a mild positive skew, but widely expected); Anthropic IPO timing (Polymarket: 1.4% by Oct 31 and 13% by Nov 15, so it most likely lands after the window [13][14]; context, not an input). Short-horizon regularities: the stock ran from $343.64 (Oct 1 close [19]) to $377.32 (+9.8%) on financing and peer read-through headlines with no Broadcom filing; partial reversal is about as likely as follow-through, and retail sentiment is 'bearish' [16], which is not a reliable contrarian signal at one month. I therefore stay near-symmetric: lognormal, median $378.5 (+0.3%), sigma 13.4% (47% / 3.5), giving P(>=377.32) = 0.509.

fair_value.method: 0.65 x P/E ($469.1 = 19x estimated FY28 EPS $24.69, built bottom-up on FY28 AI $184B) + 0.35 x DCF ($291.3 at an 11.3% CAPM-based WACC, 0.83 FCF conversion from the 8-K) = $406.9 -> $407 (+7.9% vs $377.32). Scenario-weighted value $403.0 and ladder mean ~$403 reconcile to it within 1%.

methods.inputs: FY28 revenue $238B (AI $184B + non-AI semis $18B + software $36B); semis op margin 58%, software 84% -> op income $147.4B; less $2.2B net interest; 16% tax; 4.94B shares -> EPS $24.69 x 19x = $469.1

inputs_detail.derivation: Management line of sight $230B for FY28 with supply secured [2], but Tan says the GW roadmap (~30 GW over FY27-28) is 'judged conservatively' because shells/power may slip [2]. I haircut 20% for deployment timing: 230 x 0.80 = $184B. Cross-checks: share of house 2028 base capex 184/2,255 = 8.2% vs FY27 115/1,841 = 6.2% [12], a gain backed by the Anthropic +10 GW / OpenAI >5 GW line of sight [2]; FY28/FY27 purchase commitments 72,952/52,674 = 1.385x [5] gives 115 x 1.385 = $159B as a floor-type anchor (FY28 commitments are less complete this far out).

Q4 FY26 guide ~$8.7B x 4 = $34.8B, guided to 'stabilize' despite ARR +15% [2]; ~+2%/yr for FY27-28 = ~$36B. Not raised further given VMware customer-friction signals (HN 270-point thread on VDDK download removal [15], context only).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF $101.2B (0.83 x NI $122.0B), growth 15/10/6/4% FY29-32, terminal 3%, WACC 11.3% (5.31% + 1.48 x 4.20% equity; 3.2% debt at 3.36% after tax), less net debt $35.44B, / 4.94B shares, valued at the Oct-2027 horizon

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 NI $121.97B x 0.83 FCF conversion. Conversion from the 8-K: 9M FY26 FCF $31,937M / non-GAAP NI $38,631M = 0.827; Q3 $13,665M / $16,372M = 0.835 [1].
House base customer AI capex 2027 $1,841B -> 2028 $2,255B (+22%) [12]; Tan: Google demand growing 'in 28 and 29' [2]; no capex view beyond 2028, so growth fades to terminal.

Cost of equity = 10y 5.31% [11] + beta 1.48 [9] x implied ERP 4.20% [10] = 11.53%. Debt weight = 59.42 / (1,810 + 59.42) = 3.2% (debt $59.42B = carrying $2,252M + $57,167M, 8-K balance sheet [1]; market cap $1.81T [9]); after-tax cost of debt = 4.0% weighted coupon [2] x (1 - 0.16) = 3.36%. WACC = 0.968 x 11.53% + 0.032 x 3.36% = 11.27% ~ 11.3%.
Below the 5.31% 10y nominal yield [11]; standard mature-growth assumption.

Carrying debt $2,252M + $57,167M = $59,419M less cash $23,975M = $35,444M at 2026-08-02 [1]; held to the horizon. The $29B backstop [4][6] is not charged in the base (fair value not material, nothing paid); it is in the bear case.

bear.story: AI capex digestion toward the house low case (2028 $1,265B, below 2027 [12]) or a lab customer deferring GW deployments: FY28 AI ~$120B (about flat on FY27's $115B), revenue $172B, EPS $18.16; 14x = $254 (below the 15.3x peer low, as in a cyclical de-rating) and DCF (growth 10/8/5/4%) $198.5; blend 0.65/0.35 = $235. A customer lease default would add the up-to-$29B backstop (~$6/share before rack resale) [4][6].

base.story: FY27 AI ~$115B delivered (supply secured [2]); FY28 AI $184B (80% of the $230B line of sight, 8.2% of house 2028 base capex [12]); EPS $24.69; 19x = $469, DCF $291; blend $407.

bull.story: The $230B FY28 outlook is met (Anthropic +10 GW, OpenAI >5 GW [2]; FY28 purchase commitments already $72.95B [5]), semis margin 59%: EPS $29.65 (consistent with management's 'exceed $30' [2]); 21x = $623, DCF $351; blend $528. Bull weighted above bear because the bull is management's supply-secured outlook, Broadcom beat EPS consensus in each of the last four quarters [7], and every clean 2026 hyperscaler capex guide was raised [12], while the bear needs an outright capex cut.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount rests on features that persist through Oct-2027, each from a filing or the call, not on sell-side sector calls: (1) growth at the horizon: the NTM year is then FY28, where my EPS growth is +27% ($24.69 vs $19.39 [7]), against the peers' +49.93% next-year median [8], and AVGO has no consensus beyond FY28 while Google demand is stated only for '28 and 29' [2]; (2) concentration: six XPU customers, 'four of them ... huge', with Anthropic the largest XPU customer in 2027-28 [2]; (3) balance-sheet links to customers: a ~$29B maximum undiscounted lease backstop and a $42B convertible-note facility to the same customer (undrawn) [4][6], on the first ~1 GW tranche of an XPV platform aimed at >20 GW by end-2028 [2], with further backstops unsized. The market already prices the size-matched AI-silicon cohort below the median (NVDA 15.32x, TSM 21.83x) [8]. No premium is claimed.

thesis_break_reason: $255 = 13.2x FY27 consensus EPS $19.39 [7] and 12% below the $289.96 52-week low; it matches the bear scenario's P/E price ($254). Trading there would mean the market no longer believes the supply-secured ~$115B FY27 AI revenue [2]: a cut at the 2026-12-09 or March print, a lab customer deferring GW deployments, a lease default triggering the up-to-$29B backstop [4][6], or a 2027-28 capex cut toward the house low case [12]. With 47% realized vol a move from $377 to $255 (-32%) is about a 1-sigma-ish annual move, so I would want it confirmed by a fundamental trigger rather than price alone.

reasoning: ROUND 2. I re-verified every number I use at its primary source: the Q3 FY26 8-K [1], the 10-Q notes R17/R53/R54 [4][5][6], the call transcript [2], Yahoo consensus [7], the Finviz peer table [8], StockAnalysis beta/debt [9], Damodaran's Oct-1 implied ERP [10] and the Treasury curve [11]. Following the supervisor: (a) FCF conversion is 0.83 (9M FY26 $31,937M / $38,631M), not 0.95; (b) FY28 AI is rebuilt at $184B (20% timing haircut to $230B; 8.2% of house 2028 base capex; purchase commitments give a $159B floor-type anchor); (c) EPS is built by segment ($24.69) instead of a flat 51% net margin; (d) peers are on one next-FY basis (median 23.62x, 11 peers, ARM/MU dropped, CSCO/COHR added), forward EV/EBITDA nulled; (e) unverified claims are out of every number: the Anthropic $125.2B/$161.2B commitments, the $60B bank syndication, the Polymarket $1.8T IPO-cap market and the Macquarie/UBS TPU-share notes. Where I differ from the supervisor: I use a sourced CAPM discount rate (11.3%) rather than 10.5%, so my DCF is $291 not $338 and my FV $407 not $420; I keep it because each input is sourced and the gap is disclosed (at 10.5% my FV would be ~$418). VALUE: 0.65 x $469.1 + 0.35 x $291.3 = $406.9. SCENARIOS: bear $235 (22%), base $407 (50%), bull $528 (28%), mean $403.0. LADDER: a three-component lognormal mixture centred on those scenario values (as means) with within-scenario sigmas 0.34/0.28/0.34; mixture mean ~$403 (= scenario mean; FV within 1%), median ~$381, log-sd 0.43 vs 47% realized vol (slightly below because the scenario structure carries part of the dispersion). P(>=377) = 0.51, P(>=415) = 0.41, P(>=660) = 0.07. LANE: Polymarket (IPO timing only), Hacker News engagement (low on financing stories; high on VMware customer friction, which kept my software estimate flat), Stocktwits 'bearish' retail sentiment, a Substack bull (Monte, $709 on 28.17x EV/aEBITDA, which itself expects the multiple to drift toward ~18x) and TrendForce's March report that Broadcom then guided 2027 AI to '>$100B' (now ~$115B), all context only. The in-lane share is ~6 of 19 sources because the no-unverified-claims rule forces the valuation onto filings; I flag that rather than pad the list.
